title: Unit – 4 : Session – 7 : SLO – 1  |  Multiprocessing Using IPython
sections: 1. The multiprocessing module — it spawns separate OS processes so Python code runs truly in parallel (bypassing the GIL).
2. Pool — a Pool manages a group of worker processes and distributes tasks among them.
1. [1, 4, 9] — p.map(square, [1, 2, 3]) applies square() to each element across 2 worker processes and returns the results in order.
Pool(n) creates n worker processes; the with block ensures workers are closed and joined.
map() preserves input order regardless of which process finished first.
